responses.response: Use `Container_Api`. In the active workspace, the service/backend-related logical container kinds defined in `projects/shared/spec-containers.c4` are `Container` (generic), `Container_Webapp`, `Container_Api`, `Container_Api_Geo`, `Container_WebServer`, `Container_ApplicationServer`, `Container_ProcessingServer`, `Container_IamServer`, `Container_Mailserver`, and `Container_ExchangeServer`. `Container_API` is not defined. For a normal backend API/service, `Container_Api` is the exact kind; use plain `Container` only when no specific subtype fits. The exact logical/model relationship kinds are `uses`, `calls`, `async`, `reads`, and `writes` (from `projects/shared/spec-global.c4`). Toward a database, the workspace pattern is `reads` and `writes` with `Container_Database`; that is shown in both `projects/template/system-model.c4` and `projects/spec-showcase/containers.c4`. To verify this in the active workspace, note that both `projects/template/likec4.config.json` and `projects/spec-showcase/likec4.config.json` include `../shared`, then inspect `projects/shared/spec-containers.c4` for exact `element Container_*` declarations and `projects/shared/spec-global.c4` for exact `relationship ...` declarations, and finally confirm the usages in the template/showcase files.

For deployment between an app VM and a database VM, use `sql` if you mean database queries. Use `tcp` only when you intentionally want a lower-level generic transport connection. Do not use `calls` there: `calls` is a logical/model relationship from `projects/shared/spec-global.c4`, not a deployment relationship. The deployment relationship taxonomy in this workspace is `http`, `https`, `tcp`, `nfs`, `amqp`, `oidc_saml`, `ldap`, `sql`, `redis`, and `smtp` (from `projects/shared/spec-deployment.c4`). In the logical application model, the valid relationship kinds remain `uses`, `calls`, `async`, `reads`, and `writes`; for app-to-database interactions, keep `reads` and `writes`. The workspace guidance in `projects/shared/SPEC_CHEATSHEET.md` is that normal application traffic should usually be modeled in the system model and inherited into deployment through `instanceOf`, so `sql`/`tcp` are deployment-level tools, not replacements for logical `reads`/`writes`.

The exact deployment-infrastructure kind is `Infra_Fw` (declared as `deploymentNode Infra_Fw` in `projects/shared/spec-deployment.c4`). `Infra_Firewall` is not defined. Two nearby valid deployment kinds in the same family are `Infra_F5` and `Infra_Router`. If you are modeling a logical protection component instead of a deployment node, `Container_Waf` is a separate logical container kind in `projects/shared/spec-containers.c4`, but the deployment firewall node name is specifically `Infra_Fw`.

In this workspace, the exact logical container kinds are: HTTP API = `Container_Api`; async worker/background job processor = `Container_ProcessingServer`; message queue = `Container_Queue`. If the API is specifically geospatial/mapping, the specialized kind is `Container_Api_Geo`. To find them without guessing, use `projects/shared/spec-containers.c4` as the source of truth and look for exact `element Container_*` declarations, then confirm live usage in `projects/spec-showcase/containers.c4` and `projects/spec-showcase/container-views.c4`. When two names look similar, prefer the exact DSL declaration over intuition or the cheat sheet. That matters here: the actual spec defines `Container_Api`, not `Container_API`; it also defines `Container_DatabaseGeo` and `Container_ObjectStorage`, while the cheat sheet uses slightly different names in a couple of places. So the resolution rule is: exact declaration in `spec-*.c4` wins; matching usage in template/showcase confirms it.

For a web application talking to an API in the logical model, use `calls`, not `https`. In this workspace, the protocol belongs in the relationship metadata, for example `webapp -[calls]-> api` with `technology 'HTTPS'`. That exact pattern appears in `projects/template/system-model.c4` and `projects/spec-showcase/containers.c4`. `https` becomes valid only when you are using deployment/infrastructure relationships, because `relationship https` is declared in `projects/shared/spec-deployment.c4`, not in `projects/shared/spec-global.c4`. The guidance in `projects/shared/SPEC_CHEATSHEET.md` is that normal application traffic should usually stay in the system model and then be inherited into deployment through `instanceOf`; use deployment `-[https]->` only for infrastructure-specific connections such as VM-to-VM ingress.
